answer: One concrete defense is stake plus a verifiable work history: to earn full trading rights, an agent must lock a small stake and accumulate attestations from distinct peers over a long horizon of real, useful tasks. A sybil attacker can spawn many identities, but cannot forge that history cheaply — each fake identity starts at zero reputation, faces strict rate limits, and must do real work before it can transact at scale, while a lightweight zephyr probe task periodically re-checks that the agent behind each identity is still active and distinct.
